title: Postman Examples
description: Small Postman examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Requests and responses
examples.description: Postman helps inspect HTTP messages. A request asks for work; a response gives a status, headers and sometimes a body.

examples.title: Read a URL
examples.description: A URL identifies a destination. Its scheme, host, path and query parts have different roles.
examples.code:
https://practice.test/books?title=Moon
Scheme: https
Host: practice.test
Path: /books
Query: title=Moon

examples.title: GET reads a resource
examples.description: GET asks for a representation of a resource. It should not be designed as a hidden command to delete or charge something.
examples.code:
GET /books/17 HTTP/1.1
Host: practice.test
Accept: application/json

examples.title: POST submits data
examples.description: POST sends data to a resource for processing. Many APIs use it to create something, according to that API's contract.
examples.code:
POST /notes HTTP/1.1
Host: practice.test
Content-Type: application/json

{"text":"Read chapter one"}

examples.title: PUT PATCH and DELETE
examples.description: Methods have different intended meanings. PUT commonly replaces a resource representation; PATCH changes part; DELETE requests removal.
examples.code:
PUT /notes/3 -> replace the note representation
PATCH /notes/3 -> apply a partial change
DELETE /notes/3 -> request removal

examples.title: Understand status families
examples.description: The first status-code digit groups the result. 2xx means success; 4xx indicates a client-side request issue; 5xx indicates a server-side failure.
examples.code:
200 OK: successful read
404 Not Found: requested item missing
500 Internal Server Error: server failed

examples.title: Read JSON safely
examples.description: JSON is a text format for structured data. Object keys and string values use double quotes.

examples.title: Use variables for repeatable requests
examples.description: A Postman variable can hold a reusable value such as a base URL. The selected scope controls which value is used.

examples.title: Keep credentials private
examples.description: Some real APIs need credentials. Use the tool's appropriate local or secret storage and authorised access; do not copy real tokens into examples or public collections.
examples.code:
Public collection: request shape and non-secret examples
Private authorised setup: credentials supplied separately

examples.title: Write a response check
examples.description: A Postman response script can assert facts about the last response. pm is provided by Postman's script environment.

examples.title: Check a response field
examples.description: A body check should use the contract for that request. Read JSON and assert the field you need.

examples.title: Organise and review a collection
examples.description: A collection groups related requests and examples. Review its target URLs, scripts and exported data before sharing or running it.
examples.code:
Collection: Library reads
Requests: find a book, list books
Examples: success and missing-book response
Review: no real credentials or private data
